citation_title: Requirements for provider records
evidence: "annotated case notes identifying each service or supply delivered; the case notes must be dated and either signed or initialed by the individual who provided each service"
name: Alaska
notes: Read from the official Alaska filing packet on Alaska Online Public Notices (Register 226, July 2018; filed 5/8/2018, effective 6/7/2018), which contains the adopted amendment text of 7 AAC 105.230. That packet shows only the AMENDED paragraphs — (a), (d)(5), (d)(6), (d)(7), (f), (g), (h) — so subsections (d)(1)-(d)(4) (which per secondary sources cover diagnosis, medical need, service identification, and prescription drugs) were NOT read and are not asserted here. Base rule effective 2/1/2010, Register 193. Confirmed independently at the Alaska DOH 'Waiver Provider Conditions of Participation' (Rev. 9/1/22), https://health.alaska.gov/media/hylb3ibb/provider-cop-for-waiver-and-chore-corrected-10422.pdf, which states providers must 'maintain, in accordance with 7 AAC 105.230, records that support claims for services' and may not bill 'for services that are not specified in the recipient's support plan or documented in accordance with 7 AAC 105.230.' The akleg.gov Administrative Code viewer is JavaScript/Folio-based and its backend was returning 'could not connect to pipe', so the codified text page itself was unreachable.
required_elements: Accurate financial, clinical, and other records necessary to support the services for which the provider requests payment (subsec. (a))
Stop and start times for time-based billing codes; both time-in and time-out must be documented (subsec. (d)(5))
Annotated case notes identifying each service or supply delivered (subsec. (d)(6))
Case notes dated and either signed or initialed by the individual who provided each service (subsec. (d)(6))
Records maintained contemporaneously with the service provided (subsec. (d)(7))
service_type: Residential habilitation services under the IDD waiver — rendered as family home habilitation, supported-living habilitation, group-home habilitation, or in-home support habilitation (7 AAC 130.265)
signature_rule: Case notes must be dated and either signed or initialed by the individual who provided each service. An electronic signature complying with AS 09.80 (Uniform Electronic Transactions Act) satisfies the requirement; the person named on the electronic signature and the provider bear responsibility for authenticity. No specific credential is required of the signer.
timeliness_rule: Records must be contemporaneous: 'documented in accordance with the provider's professional licensing standards, or within 72 hours from the end of the date of service, whichever is longer.' A provider may not bill for services for which records were not kept contemporaneously.

name: Alabama
notes: Alabama's DMH rule does NOT enumerate what a daily/progress note must contain. 580-5-30-.04 delegates entirely to 'ADMH Standards' (the ADMH Community Standards / DDD Operational Guidelines), which are not published in the Administrative Code and which I could not locate on a state site. 580-5-30-.11 (Review of Contracted Services) confirms ADMH monitors 'progress notes, data sheets, personal files' but likewise does not specify note content. Ala. Admin. Code r. 560-X-1-.21 (also read verbatim) requires providers to keep detailed records fully disclosing extent and cost of services, retained 3 years plus the current year. The chapter names no specific residential service type (it references '310 entities', support coordination, and HCBS waivers generically), so service_type is left null rather than guessed. DO NOT print an Alabama note-content rule number on a filed record; there isn't one in the Administrative Code.
signature_rule: Not specified in 580-5-30. Alabama Medicaid's general signature rule, Ala. Admin. Code r. 560-X-1-.18 (read verbatim at https://admincode.legislature.state.al.us/api/rule/560-X-1-.18), requires legible handwritten or compliant electronic/digital signatures that clearly identify the provider performing the billed service; illegible signatures need a signature log or attestation; 'auto-authentication'/'auto-signature' systems and 'signed but not read' are not acceptable.

Department on Disability Services guidance document 'Medicaid Waiver Services Documentation Requirements' (February 16, 2024), read verbatim at https://dds.dc.gov/sites/default/files/dc/sites/dds/page_content/attachments/Medicaid%20Waiver%20Services%20Documentation%20Requirements-%20FINAL%202.16.2024.pdf, which cites 29 DCMR §1909.2(m) and 29 DCMR § 9006.2(m). The health or behavioral events or change in status that is not typical to the person

Evidence of all community integration and inclusion activities attended by the person and related to the person's ISP goals, and for each, answers to 'What did the person like about the activity?' and 'What did the person not like about the activity?'
The start time and end time of each shift for any services received
The signature of the Direct Support Professional (DSP)

The matters requiring follow-up on the part of the Waiver service provider or DDS

Date(s) of service (day, month, and year)
Time of service (begin time and end time, using either AM/PM or military time)

service_type: Residential Habilitation (ResHab), provided in a licensed/certified home and the surrounding community; four SIS-based tiers. Related in-home services are Personal Assistance/Habilitation (PAB) and Community Learning Service – Individual (CLS-Ind).
